blocks.content: Article 32 is the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it.

items: frequently tested: Identify which amendments added specific words to the Preamble vs. those that introduced Fundamental Duties.
Distinguish clearly between the 73rd Amendment (Panchayati Raj / Rural) and 74th Amendment (Municipalities / Urban).
Remember that Fundamental Rights are justiciable, whereas Fundamental Duties and Directive Principles are non-justiciable.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Constituent Assembly took nearly three years to finalize and adopt the Constitution of India.
Article 32 guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies and enables citizens to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 added the terms 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.
Fundamental Duties were incorporated into Part IV-A via Article 51A based on the Swaran Singh Committee recommendations.
